overview: This Senate resolution recognizes May as Jewish American Heritage Month, a time to celebrate the contributions of Jewish Americans, whose community in the United States dates back to 1654. It reviews the history of the observance and cites reports from Jewish organizations and the FBI showing that antisemitic incidents and hate crimes reached record levels after the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack on Israel. The resolution calls on elected officials, faith leaders, and community leaders to condemn and counter all acts of antisemitism and to educate the public about Jewish Americans' contributions. It also expresses a commitment to the safety and dignity of American Jews at work, on campuses, at synagogues, and at home. It does not change any law or spending, and the Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on May 22, 2025.
for: Supporters say that with antisemitic incidents at record highs, it matters for the Senate to celebrate Jewish Americans' contributions and to call clearly on leaders to confront hatred.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and changes no law or spending, so it adds no new protections or resources to address the rise in antisemitic incidents it describes.
